description.narrative:
Oxfam has been working in Niger since 1992 and has had continuous representation in the Zinder region for over a decade, leading tothe establishment of a base over three years ago. Currently, Oxfam is implementing a development project there with funding from DGD Belgium, in which, due to the fragility of the area and the recurrence of natural shocks, a crisis modification mechanism has beenplanned to preserve the gains made against these contingencies. Moreover, we are targeting the municipalities of Dakoussa and Timini, to enable us to have the financial capacity to cover all households affected by flooding in your intervention villages in order to avoid the risk of finding or frustration that could arise from exclusive support for beneficiaries of the DGD Development project through the crisis modifier (complementarity). To implement this project, Oxfam will work in partnership with the NGO Garkua. NGO Garkua is a national NGO that has worked with Oxfam in Niger for around four years in both development and humanitarian sectors. This partnership facilitates community engagement, acceptance of Oxfam and its partners as well as the localization of our interventions taking into account local capacities and opportunities. Garkua has proven capacities inthe field of cash transfers, but also in foodsecurity and protection. The organization has a solid base in the Zinder Region and an ongoing funding agreement with Oxfam in Niger, for the Zinder Region (as part of the DGD Development Project on which theactivation of the "crisis modifier" is triggered to support the response to this flood crisis). Oxfam has proven capacities in the conduct of cash transfers including evaluation tools (feasibility of Cash, Market Monitoring) and currently has a frameworkcontract for cash transfers with a national money transfer agencynamed NITA. Oxfam in Niger has implemented and continues to implement Cash Transfer Projects with funding from various donors such as ECHO, GFFO, SIDA, DANIDA, AECID, etc.
In NIger, Oxfam and its partners intervene in all vital sectors, particularly Food and Nutritional security, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene, and emergency Protection, in conflict-sensitive approaches to reduce the risk of exacerbating conflicts and a single program (One Program approach) combining life-saving activities with advocacy for the protection and promotion of human rights. We also collaborate with local authorities, technical services as well as local service providers andsuppliers to whom we are linked, forsome, by framework contracts facilitating the rapid acquisition of goods and services. Also, inorder to give itself the chance to conduct activities safely without harming and exposing staff or the reputation of the institution, Oxfam in Niger adopts anapproach in a safe programming approach. Oxfam in Niger also has security and prevention policies with standard operating procedures to reduce security risks and preserve the dignity of the people targeted by our intervention. In a concern for accountability to the various stakeholders, Oxfam in Niger, as part of these interventions, sets up local complaint management mechanisms called complaint management committees whose members chosen by their peers in village assemblies are trained and equipped to play the role assigned to them. In addition, a toll-free number is provided to communities to file their complaints or report any suspicion of reprehensible behavior on the part of Oxfam staff, their colleagues or partners. With qualified and experienced staff in all the areas mentioned above, Oxfam and its partners have extensive experience in emergency response throughout the country." For this intervention, Oxfam will work with a local structure well established in the area, namely the NGO Garkua. It isa national NGO that has been implementing humanitarian and development projects since 2016 in the sectors of food security, community-based protection, malnutrition prevention and social cohesion in the regions of Zinder, Tillabéri, Dosso and Diffa in Niger. Garkua has a strong community base and has built good partnership relationships with the authorities through various projects in Zinder: PACPS, PASPR, CSP/PAM, ACPI/UNICEF, DGD DEV/OXFAM. It has been working with Oxfam since 2020 and is currently implementing funding in partnership with Oxfam in Zinder. Like Oxfam, GARKUA is an active player in coordination bodies at the national and regional levels, such as clusters, technical working groups, the Cash Working Group, etc.

participating-org.narrative: The Nigerien Association for Sustainable Development (ANDD Garkua) is a Nigerien non-profit, non-political and non-confessional NGOcreated by Order n ° 0154 / MISPD / ACR / DGAPJ / DLP of 24 February 2016. Garkua is present in six of the eight regions of Niger. It aims to promote the rights of grassroots communities.
